claims.statement: NBRC's 'Respiratory Therapy Examination Detailed Content Outline' (effective Jan 2027) is already published as a PDF on nbrc.org, dated Oct 10, 2025, laying out task/cognitive-level specs for a Breadth of Knowledge portion (100 items) and a Depth of Clinical Judgment portion (60 items).
claims.source_excerpt: The Examination contains 160 items divided into two portions... Breadth of Knowledge portion contains 100 items... Depth of Clinical Judgement portion contains 60 items.

claims.statement: The new RTE is 185 total multiple-choice items (160 scored + 25 pretest) over 4 hours, vs the old TMC's 160 items (140 scored + 20 pretest) over 3 hours -- 25 more total items and 1 more hour of seat time than TMC.
claims.source_excerpt: The Respiratory Therapy Examination consists of 185 multiple-choice items (160 scored and 25 pretest) taken over a 4-hour period.

claims.statement: Inside the RTE's 60-item Depth of Clinical Judgment portion, items split into two named types with fixed counts: Information Gathering (20 items, 'choose what to assess or interpret') and Decision Making (40 items, 'decide what to add, modify, continue, or discontinue'); items also carry Setting quotas (46 in-hospital / 14 outside-hospital) and a Patient Age quota (15-18 min/max neonatal-or-pediatric items) -- none of this granular quota structure exists in the old TMC outline.
claims.source_excerpt: Information Gathering _Choose what to assess or interpret information_ 20 / Decision Making _Decide what to add, modify, continue, or discontinue_ 40 / Total 60 ... In a hospital 46 / Outside a hospital 14

claims.statement: The NBRC has stated the RTE is built entirely from independent multiple-choice items -- the branching CSE simulation format is fully retired, and there is no public indication of select-all-that-apply items; clinical reasoning is instead assessed through longer, scenario-based MCQ stems.
claims.source_excerpt: Are all RTE questions multiple choice? Yes... Will the RTE have CSE-style simulations? No. The branching CSE format is retired.

claims.statement: Per Lindsey Jones' own analysis of the released NBRC content outline, the RTE blueprint added roughly 100 new topics and dropped about 40 topics that existed on the TMC outline -- a concrete content delta, not just a structural one.
claims.source_excerpt: Our initial evaluation of the NBRC Respiratory Therapy Examination (RTE) detailed content outline (the matrix) shows 100 new topics that have been added and 40 topics that have disappeared.
